expectation: Membrane ring on nearly all nucleated cells: epithelium, stroma, immune cells and endothelium. Dense, crisp honeycomb outlines that follow the cells, not the tissue outline. Tumour regions may have patches where the stain is lost or dim.
observed: A: both gut-like sections stained throughout, with haze off the tissue. B: a sharp membrane honeycomb over the epithelium. C: crisp lateral membranes on columnar crypt cells, with a dark lumen. D: blurred haze. E: membrane rings, and some green cells sit on CD31 vessels.
why: B and C show sharp membrane rings that outline each cell, which is what this marker should look like on all nucleated cells; the edge haze and the blurred D do not change that.
notes: HLAA gives crisp membrane outlines on epithelial cells, both in sheets and in crypts, as expected for a marker on all nucleated cells. The haze off the tissue and the blurred close-up at D are artefacts.
